sentences.text: The system measures operational performance against approved service objectives and documented fleet baselines.
Availability is reported for each turbine and for the fleet, with planned maintenance and forced outages classified separately.
Energy production measures include delivered energy, production lost during downtime, and the duration of grid-related restrictions.
Maintenance performance is assessed through work completion time, repeat work, overdue tasks, and the proportion of work completed as planned.
Safety performance measures include reported events, completion of required controls, and timely closure of corrective actions.
Performance definitions identify the source data, calculation method, reporting interval, and accountable owner for each measure.
The SCADA Gateway provides operational records used to assess turbine availability and production trends.
The Nacelle Condition Monitor supports assessment of equipment condition and emerging degradation.
The Offshore Substation is reviewed for operational availability and the frequency and duration of equipment interruptions.
The Fleet Dispatch Console provides a fleet-level view of operating status and response to emerging constraints.
The Maintenance Planning Engine supports review of planned work, resource demand, and maintenance completion performance.
Performance results are reviewed at regular operational meetings and escalated when approved thresholds are exceeded.
The Control Engineer examines significant operational deviations and records the technical findings for review.
Reliability reviews consider failure frequency, failure duration, recurrence, and the operational consequences of each event.
Review teams distinguish equipment faults from external causes such as access limitations, weather conditions, and grid restrictions.
Failure analyses use available operating history, inspection findings, and maintenance records to identify credible causes.
Corrective actions are assigned an owner, due date, and verification method before they are tracked to closure.
The Duty Planner uses reliability findings to adjust work priorities and planned maintenance intervals when justified.
Lessons learned from maintenance campaigns and significant events are captured in a form that can be applied across the fleet.
The Field Supervisor provides feedback on whether revised procedures and controls are practical during offshore work.
The Warehouse System uses recurring failure and repair information to inform review of critical spares and replenishment assumptions.
The Cybersecurity Analyst reviews performance records for evidence that cybersecurity controls affect operational availability or recovery.
Changes to performance definitions or reporting logic are controlled so that trends remain comparable over time.
Proposed reliability improvements are assessed for safety, technical feasibility, resource needs, and expected operational benefit.
Approved improvements are monitored after implementation to confirm that they deliver the intended result and do not introduce adverse effects.
The operational concept is reviewed periodically so that performance measures and lessons learned continue to reflect actual operating experience.
